title.value: What the Pits Say Before the Belt Does

description.value: Fixed forecasting phrases held by the weather watch and taught in the same words to every trainee, each tied to a reading of the flank pits and to a stretch of coast. They are recited rather than reasoned about, and a watch who paraphrases them is corrected.

content.value:
Left flank and not the right: it is coming north, and you have six hours, and the racks come down first.

Both flanks together and slow: it is standing where it is. Work, but work inside the second line.

Both flanks together and fast: it is not standing anywhere. Call it.

Nothing in the pits and the water gone flat: it is behind you. That one is not a warning, it is a description.

And when the sky opens at the belt edge on a still night, that is not weather, that is the skimmers coming down, and the calendar is named for them and not the other way round.
